entry.title: Now That's A Thinker
entry.summary: I admit it. I think a lot. Now, some fools out…
entry.content:
I admit it.

I think a lot.

Now, some fools out there will try and convince you that thinking isn't action.

But it is.

It's an action.

Patience, planning, and strategy sometimes confuses those who just jump at the first shiny object then the next.

Then the next.

Squirrel!!!

🐿

Why are we doing this?

That's a fine question.

How are we doing this?

Finer.

What are we doing?

Best question yet.

Who and when are probably something to consider, too.

All require thinking.

Thinking is an action.

People in this hustle culture or whatever the heck we call it today just brag about how they did this or that but they never stopped to think.

They just kept doing this or that.

That or this.

Look how great I turned out, is their schtick.

But I think, they turned out terribly.

At least for me.

For me.

You do you.

I don't want what they have or they claim they got.

I seek something different.

I don't have many heroes, but they all seem to do a lot of contemplating.

Which is just a fancy word for thinking.

Alright stop.

Collaborate and listen.

What are you doing?

Right now.

Why are you doing it?

How are you doing?

Who are you doing it with and for?

When will you decide to do something else?

Do you think it's a good idea?

Do you like your answers?

What are you going to do about it?

entry.title: Horizontal
entry.summary: Algorithms, man. Algorithms. It occurs to me that I let them…
entry.content:
Algorithms, man.

Algorithms.

It occurs to me that I let them feed me.

Too much.

Like I'm reclining.

And they got grapes.

🍇

I must admit, I like when they feed me a small creator I never heard of.

Talking about a subject I've been digging into.

One with a small, but dedicated, following.

It's like finding a small town's genius.

The internet can be staggering.

Bigger than any city in the land.

But it's also full of all these tiny, hidden, communities.

Not sleepy at all, though.

Quite lively really.

More my vibe.

I've watched and followed these for a while now.

Marveling at how they don't seem to grow.

They don't change.

And they're fine with it.

Maybe not happy, but fine with it.

I wonder how these people got here.

I wonder if they were fed grapes like me.

The internet, people say, has died.

But they don't know sheet.

Never have.

All of this to say, don't let it feed you forever.

Start using them fingers to type.

Search.

Query.

Hunt.

Type in something and write .com and go there.

See what happens.

Although that sounds like a lot of work.

Fine, fine.

Are those fresh figs?

Lay off me, I'm starving.

entry.title: Cherish Is The Word I Use To Describe
entry.summary: Man. I wrote a few drafts but erased 'em. I tried…
entry.content:
Man.

I wrote a few drafts but erased 'em.

I tried to dig deep.

But didn't like what I struck.

So I shoveled it back.

Leveled the ground. 

Couldn't even tell I dug.

Life is this dance between nostalgia and vision and the ever present.

All happening at once.

Past, present, future.

All three are very real, though.

Which is the realist?

Realest.

I used to always think in the future.

Never the past.

But it occurs to me, that perhaps there's more past than future.

At least for me.

And thus I have a lot to look back upon, rather than look forward to.

But I do.

I look forward to a lot.

It's what long game players do.

Even old(ish) ones.

I wear my future lens with the knowledge that every good moment or not so good I get the privilege to experience is because I'm still here.

Because I still walk the earth.

The honor of life.

Of living.

Cherish every second.

As a husband and father, sometimes I just want peace and quiet.

As a husband and father, I know sometimes that's just a pipe dream.

So I take chaos and loudness.

And embrace them.

Give them both a big kiss.

And say, thank you, God.

For headphones.

And all the other stuff.

In between.

Now, shhh...

entry.title: Had Me @ Heads Carolina
entry.summary: You want to create a hit? What's that now? A hit…
entry.content:
You want to create a hit?

What's that now?

A hit song.

Top 40 or whatever the metric is these days.

The hard way is to come up with something original.

The easy way is to take an old hit.

Just take it.

Either remake it.

Or make a new song with the old song inside it.

Featuring a 90s 2000s star.

Like Hootie Darius or Jo Dee (Messina, not Dumars - both legends, though).

Talk about Carolina beaches.

Gotta be Carolina.

And falling in love.

It'll be a hit.

I guar-on-tee.

It's pandering.

Lowest common denominator.

You say.

Yes, yes, I suppose it is.

Low hanging fruit.

But nostalgia renewed, man.

Holy crap, do I dig it.

A time machine.

Forwards and back.

I like those.

You want to make a hit?

Look behind you.

You had me at Hootie.

And the hits just keep on comin'.

entry.title: How You All Are
entry.summary: I cook a mean kimchi jigae. You know, kimchi stew? There's…
entry.content:
I cook a mean kimchi jigae.

You know, kimchi stew?

There's always a fresh pot of it on the stove.

I don't add an extra j to jigae (jjigae) like you're supposed to because it makes no sense.

What the heck is a jjigae?

One J.

Did I stutter?

One.

Chill.

The secret to a mean kimchi jigae is bacon.

Two slices.

Three or four if you nasty.

Are you nasty?

Now you can fry it in advance.

Before you add kimchi.

Or you can just throw it in a lot of water and let 'er boil.

I tend to boil the bacon.

The fat of the bacon just melts into the broth.

Kimchi.

Garlic (sometimes I skip this).

Dashi.

Sesame oil.

Salt.

Love.

Heat.

Time.

That's it.

I couldn't tell you how long I cook the thing.

I just keep an eye on it.

Kimchi gotta be tender.

Bacon gotta disintegrate off the spoon.

You taste.

You sip.

You sample.

Needs a little more time.

Don't we all?

🍲

Kimchi jigae is a side dish.

Gotta have meat and rice with it.

But meat and rice ain't the same without kimchi jigae.

A side character who's really the star.

Meat can be boring.

Steak.

Chicken.

Beef.

So can rice.

Steamed white.

Maybe a pinch of black rice to make it purple.

But the jigae?

Heck no.

No boring jigaes allowed in this house.

Mother mother shines.

To side characters who are really, secretly, maybe not so secretly, the stars.

I see you.

⭐

entry.title: Brokes And Wholes
entry.summary: What do I talk about today. I never know. Have I…
entry.content:
What do I talk about today.

I never know.

Have I run out of things to say?

Maybe.

Maybe.

We all know energy and time are the true forms of currency.

But I'm going to add another.

No, not paper and metal.

I'm going to say your soul.

Your character.

Your integrity.

Your backbone.

Your ability to look yourself in the mirror.

And like who you see.

Not what.

I would say pride but some say that's not a good thing to call it.

🦁

As broke as I've been, I would like to think I never sold that.

Never sold out.

And the crowd goes mild!

When you trade soul for cash, that's the one that breaks you.

And I don't want you to break.

Or be broke, for that matter.

But broke and whole is better than rich and broken.

Make sense?

Make cents?

Make sense.

Make cents.

Look in the mirror.

Right now.

Who, not what, do you see?

If you can look and smile, deeply, genuinely, you have won.

Man, do I look funny.

😋

And if you frown or weep, well, there's still time.

You have the energy.

I hope.

I hope.

I'm not talking superficial surfaces here.

Go inside.

Dig deep.

First principles.

Foundation.

I bet there's something still there.

Untouched.

Unsold.

Good.

And priceless.

Some of the best babyfaces were at first the worst heels.

To those who struggle, with their souls intact.

I salute you.

Coke zero in hand.

Better broke and whole.

Don't you always say in an A or B choice, to choose C?

Don't be an arse, stay whole.

entry.title: It's Not My Fault Being the Biggest and the Strongest. I Don't Even Exercise.
entry.summary: I don't lift anymore. Now, if you told me that five…
entry.content:
I don't lift anymore.

Now, if you told me that five years ago. 

I wouldn't believe you.

I'd say, "That means I'm no longer on this timeline."

And that would be true.

Kinda true.

Almost.

I used to call lifting weights "training."

In that I'd say, "I gotta go train."

Which confused some normal folk.

Silly normal folk.

Train for what?

Nothing.

Just something I do.

But that's what I called it.

I didn't lift iron because I loved it.

Even though I did.

I lifted because I had to take the edge off.

Do you know what I mean?

I had so much fire and fury that I had to spend it on something.

Expend it.

If I didn't, I would explode.

The gym was my sanctuary.

A place I would go to worship, oddly.

A spiritual place.

I would blast my ear drums with special playlists.

My ears thank me today for that.

Thanks, Al.

But I no longer train.

Due to many reasons.

Age.

Near death experiences.

And, strangely, the fire's dimmer.

You could call it getting old(ish).

I'd like to think it's wisdom. Wissmart.

But it's because my body doesn't like lifting anymore.

Or at least right now.

I've punished it for many decades.

It's time to do what it asks.

It's the least I can do, after getting me through all I put it through.

Like an old car you treated like crap, but loved every day.

I built up a suit of armor because I wanted to protect myself.

I suppose there are better ways to do that.

If you'd have told me I don't train anymore, I would have called you a liar.

You might still be one, but not on this.

⛰

"Look, are you just fiddling around with me or what?"

"I just want you to feel you're doing well."

entry.title: Head in Alpha Centauri
entry.summary: If you told me this is all a dream, I'd believe…
entry.content:
If you told me this is all a dream, I'd believe you.

That I am dreaming.

Sure, I been through some sheet.

We all have.

And news flash, we'll all go through more.

That's the lens I use now.

Al been through some sheet.

Blessed with a miracle (or three).

For the honor and privilege of going through more sheet.

Oh snap, you bolded that. Must be important.

The honor and privilege of sheet.

More of it.

Sheet, that is.

In case you didn't know.

And so I thank God.

For the challenges.

Because I'm pretty sure I got lucky.

I get lucky.

I am lucky.

Every obstacle.

It's why I'm still here.

Every incident.

Why I still breathe.

Every sheet.

Thank you for letting me be here to help.

I can't bring it like I used to.

I suppose I needed some tuning down, anyways.

But I'm still here, ya'll.

Lost a step, to gain two.

Can't read as well, so I listen more.

Kinda.

Not really.

I can still write.

By touch if needed.

My old law partner used to stand and pace and dictate.

i suppose I could do that.

To ordeals.

And the blessings to be here to face them.

Don't wake me yet.

Life's just getting to the best part.

entry.title: I Don't Think You're Ready For This Jelly
entry.summary: Marketing. I wrestle with this idea. This idea of marketing. And…
entry.content:
Marketing.

I wrestle with this idea.

This idea of marketing.

And marketers.

Icky.

And how, so much of their tactical "advice" seems to be manipulative.

Convincing someone they should want something.

Whether they truly want it or not.

And whether or not it would truly add any value (to the buyer).

I always market the other way.

Build it and they will come.

Marketing by not marketing.

This is the way that the experts will tell you will fail.

Because they tend to be all about the numbers.

The braggy numbers.

But here's the thing.

I think I do market.

Just want to do it my way.

You on the fence about buying?

Fine.

Fine.

Go home and think on it.

I ain't begging.

Or twisting your arm.

When I worked at a gym in my youth, we weren't given a commission for memberships. 

So there was no incentive to sign up members.

At least financially.

So I'd just show folks around.

No hard sells.

Just a true enthusiasm for what we offered.

And you know what?

I sold a lot of memberships.

You should have received a commission.

I didn't have to give them a free gimmick.

Or woo them in with introductory prices.

One flat rate.

Discount for seniors and students.

Folks appreciated that.

And that's who I wanted to serve.

Those who disliked being sold.

I closed because I didn't close.

It's always worked.

And it always will.

For some.

This is an interesting filter.

Because some people need to be hard sold.

And some appreciate the opposite.

It is manipulative in the sense that some are wooed by the intrigue of not being sold to.

Who do you want?

Too many of us focus on the numbers.

I think we should focus on the quality of who those numbers represent.

So much of life is getting the decision right once.

And choosing that choice every day of your life.

The amount of trash that becomes something "big" is probably at its all-time high.

Folks out here selling souls.

Their own and others.

But I'm just an old(ish) curmudgeon.

Ain't trying to sell sheet.

For greenbacks or salvation.

But if I was, I'd probably turn a lot of you away.

Terrible marketing, I know.

But eh, what can I say?

entry.title: You Name You
entry.summary: I don't believe in weak ends. Weekends. I believe in strong…
entry.content:
I don't believe in weak ends.

Weekends.

I believe in strong beginnings.

I will not go quietly.

What we name things is as important as what they actually are.

I wish it wasn't the case.

Sorta.

I sorta wish that.

That you could call something wonderful a turd and people would still think it wonderful.

But I don't think it's so.

To have a name is to be.

Just make sure you name you.
